title: population-line.v1
description: ONE LINE of a batch decisioning population file — `s3://colx-dev-batch/population/date=<D>/run=<runId>/population.jsonl`, one JSON object per line, no wrapping array, so a million-row population streams without ever being held in memory (plan §7 DEC-10, ANA-10). Each line is self-contained: the whole context travels with the subject, so a batch decision is reproducible from the population file alone, months later, with no upstream call. The population is built by dbt/Snowflake (`int_collection_eligibility`, A§46) shaped to exactly these fields; the context-parity test asserts that the Snowflake-built context equals the online context builder's output for sampled accounts, which is the guard against the top project risk — a simulation that disagrees with production because the two read different data. `legacyDecision` is present only in migration and parity populations (A§87–88).

subject.description: Batch key for the line, duplicated at line level so a worker can dedupe on `(batch_id, account_id)` and report an error line without parsing the whole context. The worker asserts it equals `context.subject` field for field and rejects the line otherwise — two disagreeing subjects on one line make the decision unattributable.

context.description: The full decision context for this subject, as of the population's business date. Referenced by absolute `$id` rather than copied, so a batch line and an online decision are validated by the same schema and cannot drift.

legacyDecision.description: OPTIONAL — what the legacy engine decided for this subject on this data. Omitted (never null) outside migration work. Its only consumer is the shadow-run comparator with `strategyB: "LEGACY"` (DEC-13), which diffs the new engine against it and categorises every difference per A§88 — the point being that 100% agreement is not the goal, but every disagreement must have an explanation.

decision.description: Legacy outcome normalised into the platform's four-value vocabulary by the migration mapper, so the two engines are comparable at all. The mapping itself is part of the migration work (A§87) and is recorded there, not here.

treatmentCode.description: OPTIONAL — mapped legacy treatment code; present when `decision` is TREAT.

channel.description: OPTIONAL — mapped legacy channel; present when `decision` is TREAT.

reasonCodes.description: Legacy reason codes, mapped where a mapping exists and carried verbatim where none does. Shape is enforced (SCREAMING_SNAKE) but registry membership is NOT required for this field alone: the legacy vocabulary is not ours to close, and dropping an unmapped code would hide exactly the differences a parity run exists to find. Every reason code the PLATFORM emits must be in registries/reason-codes.v1.json (CON-7 cross-checks it).

allOf.title: a legacy TREAT names a treatment and a channel
allOf.description: A legacy "contact this customer" with no channel cannot be compared against a new-engine decision, so it is rejected at population-build time rather than counted as a mystery diff.
